rule.name: card_number_validation
rule.description: Many small online payments on a stolen card within a short time frame.
rule.rationale: Card testers validate stolen numbers with very small charges in rapid succession; genuine customers rarely make five micro-payments at three merchants in an hour.

rule.name: account_takeover
rule.description: Online order from a new device with a significantly higher amount than usual.
rule.rationale: Account takeover fraudsters use new devices to make large, untraceable purchases; legitimate customers typically spend within their usual limits.

rule.name: unfamiliar_device_abroad_purchase
rule.description: Online purchase over $500 from an unfamiliar device with an IP address from a different country.
rule.rationale: Online fraudsters often use unfamiliar devices to bypass security; IP addresses from different countries indicate a foreign location.

rule.name: recently_opened_sudden_spending
rule.description: Accounts opened within the last 30 days with a sudden spike in spending over $10,000 within 24 hours.
rule.rationale: Fraudsters often open new accounts to test the security of the bank and then immediately spend a large amount of money within a short period to see if the bank can detect the fraud.

rule.name: synthetic_identity
rule.description: Accounts under 30 days old spending heavily on gift cards or electronics.
rule.rationale: Synthetic identity fraudsters use new accounts to quickly buy expensive items that can be resold; legitimate customers tend to spend more gradually.

rule.name: card_travel_only_aft
rule.description: Card used in person in a foreign country only a few hours after it was used at home.
rule.rationale: Cardholders use their cards only in person in foreign countries; the short time between use at home and abroad is impossible for legitimate travel.

rule.name: skimmed_card_abroad
rule.description: Multiple ATM cashouts in a foreign country on the same day with the same card.
rule.rationale: Skimmed cards are typically used abroad at ATMs; multiple transactions in different countries indicate a fraudster's attempt to cover up the origin of the stolen card.
